QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_41

question.text: Per the 'Industry Best Practices' section, the manager of a Cat I/II AIF should typically:

answer.text: Identify Key Persons / Key Executives of the fund and take Keyman Insurance as well as Indemnity Insurance
Rely only on verbal succession plans
Disclose key-person identities only after a vacancy arises
Avoid naming any key person in the PPM

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook's Industry Best Practices section recommends identifying Key Persons / Key Executives and taking both Keyman Insurance and Indemnity Insurance, with Key Persons required to inform investors of any situation that substantially affects their dedication to the fund. The Trap: Verbal succession plans, hiding key-person identities, and only post-vacancy disclosure all conflict with the transparency expectation in the workbook. Note: The best-practice recommendation appears on page 249; the workbook does not provide cost benchmarks for the insurance policies or prescribe PPM-annexure placement.
